issues.description: Field type mismatch for the saloon's shared inventory: The problem statement (UML and textual requirements) refers to a class named `Stock` that provides methods like add(String), take(String), findStockIngredient(String), addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) and emptyStock(). In the provided code, the actual shared field in SealSaloon is declared as type `Inventory` (static final Inventory stock) and the concrete implementation of those methods is in Inventory.java. There is also an empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java file in the template/solution. This mismatch (problem statement expects a `Stock` type, code exposes `Inventory`) will confuse students about which type to implement or use and whether they must rename or re-implement classes to satisfy the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the declared type of the shared inventory across the problem statement, template, and solution. Two valid options: (A) Rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (move/rename Inventory.java -> Stock.java and update all references, then remove the empty Stock.java), preserving the implemented methods; or (B) Update the problem statement and UML to refer to `Inventory` instead of `Stock`. Ensure the SealSaloon.static stock field's type and all textual UML references match the chosen name so students can map requirements to provided code without extra renaming.

issues.description: Naming inconsistency for the same conceptual entity: The exercise text and UML use the identifier `Stock` for the saloon's inventory class, but the provided codebase defines and uses a class named `Inventory` (and SealSaloon declares its static field as type `Inventory`). An (empty) Stock.java file is present in the template/solution, which further obscures whether students should work with `Stock` or `Inventory`. This mismatch in the canonical name of the inventory class is likely to confuse students when implementing or reading the starter code and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the Inventory class/file to Stock (and remove or replace the empty Stock.java), updating all references in SealSaloon, tests, and documentation; or (B) revise the problem statement and UML to use `Inventory` everywhere instead of `Stock`. Prefer making the code and the UML/text match exactly so students do not need to perform a rename to reconcile the artifacts.
